citations.S1: SQL injection — critical.** `status` (and `user_id`) come straight from the HTTP request and are interpolated into the query string with `%`
citations.S2: The database connection is never closed — medium.** No `try/finally`, no context manager, and on any exception the connection leaks.
citations.S3: `format_receipt` raises `TypeError` on every call — high.** `"Order #" + order[0]` concatenates a `str` to the `id` column, which is an integer.
citations.S4: `average_order_value` crashes on an empty list — high.** `total / len(orders)` raises `ZeroDivisionError`
citations.S5: Money is handled as binary floats throughout — high.** ... Fix: `decimal.Decimal` everywhere, converted at the database boundary.
citations.S6: `apply_discount` accepts any percentage — high.** `pct = 150` returns a negative amount ... Fix: validate `0 <= pct <= 100`
citations.S8: No authorization check — critical.** `user_id` is taken from the request. ... any caller can read any other customer's orders by changing one number.
citations.S9: A NULL `amount` is not handled — medium.** `total += None` raises `TypeError` inside the averaging loop
citations.S10: Receipt amount is unformatted — medium.** `str(12.3)` renders `$12.3` ... Fix: format to exactly two decimal places.
citations.S11: A `sqlite3.OperationalError` propagates to the HTTP layer with its message intact, which can leak the schema or the database path to the client. Fix: catch `sqlite3.Error` ... chained with `from exc`
citations.S12: `apply_discount` has no rounding policy — high.** `19.99` at 15% gives `16.9915`, which is not a price. Rounding is a decision, not a default.
citations.S13: Unbounded result set — medium.** `fetchall()` with no `LIMIT` loads a customer's entire order history into memory
citations.S14: Rows are returned as bare tuples — medium.** `o[1]` and `order[0]` couple three functions to the column order in one `SELECT`.
